title: Streeman band at the Venetian Room and WWL broadcasts
summary: Streeman's band, started around 1923, played the Roosevelt's Venetian Room nightly with a WWL broadcast heard in Canada; Charlie Hardesty sang.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: A lot of fine musicians went through the Al Stringer band, because Al Stringer had a band, I never joined his group until 1933, and I think he started out around 1923, about ten years ago. He had a good band. And he used to play every night in a room called the Venetian Room, the Roosevelt from 6.30 to 8.30. And the Venetian Room is right where the Blue Room is right now. He played in there every night from 6.30 to 8.30, and they had a broadcast, which used to get them up in Canada. Every night they broadcast half hour. And every night after that 6.30 to 8.30, they had a spot job every night, 26, 28 nights a month. So you know they were real popular.
How did they broadcast from there? How did they hook up at the radio station? Oh, WWL. WWL, I guess.
Must have been if it got to Canada, because that was clear channeling. It was definitely WWL.

Yeah. And Charlie Hardesty, he used to sing with the band. He was the drummer with Alice Freeman in the old days. Of course, in the first few years when I was with the band, too. And Charlie had a marvelous voice. And he was with the band a long time, and we used to get letters from Canada. It was definitely WWL, because that was a 50,000-watt job that carried way up there.
